No project or migration framework in this directory, so this is plain PostgreSQL against an assumed `users` table. I have not run it.

```sql
BEGIN;

ALTER TABLE users
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS first_name text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS last_name  text;

-- ponytail: naive split, first word = first name, the rest = last name
-- ("Mary Ann Smith" -> "Mary" / "Ann Smith"). Fix odd ones by hand.
-- ponytail: single UPDATE locks every row it touches; batch by id range on big tables.
UPDATE users
SET first_name = substring(full_name from '\S+'),
    last_name  = substring(full_name from '^\s*\S+\s+(.*\S)')
WHERE first_name IS NULL
  AND last_name  IS NULL
  AND full_name  IS NOT NULL;

COMMIT;

-- check: should return 0
SELECT count(*) FROM users
WHERE full_name ~ '\S' AND first_name IS NULL;
```

It is safe to run twice because `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` is a no-op the second time, and the `UPDATE` only touches rows where both new columns are still NULL. A rerun therefore won't overwrite names that were backfilled or edited since.

Single-word names get a NULL `last_name`, and blank `full_name` values leave both columns NULL.

Skipped: dropping `full_name`. Add it as a separate migration once the app no longer reads that column, since the drop is the one step you can't undo.
